correctness.rationale: The rooted-tree inverse Green kernel sums common path resistances. A rank-one comparison across a cut yields \(J(v)-J(u)=r\mathcal B(u,v)\); decomposition at consecutive path edges gives \(\mathcal B(v,w)-\mathcal B(u,v)=4S(C,v)+r[a^2+(c+d)^2]+s[(a+c)^2+d^2]>0\) for all positive resistances. This strict increase proves every local minimum is global and at most two adjacent ties. Explicit two-pass recurrences recover every objective value in linear arithmetic time. Fresh exact verification checked 3,798 separately calculated rational grounded inverses and every simple path in 635 test trees. Finite tests are corroboration; the theorem follows from exact algebra.

originality.rationale: The new mathematical implication is strict increasing signed comparison brackets on every path of every positive weighted tree, yielding at most two adjacent optimal vertices and an O(n) exact algorithm. Inspected primary 2014–2019 literature covers first-order centrality/paths or the general second-order formula and approximation; none of those inspected statements imply this strong all-tree exact property. Accessible historical results include narrower paths, not the universal strict-edge-gradient theorem. Special-source and incomplete-index coverage remain explicit risks.

value.rationale: A structural universal minimizer classification and exact O(n) optimization for every positively weighted tree resolves a natural one-leader second-order coherence problem. It excludes spurious local minima, classifies all ties, and differs substantively from the standard weighted-tree median: resistances (100,1,1,1) on a five-vertex path move the inverse-square optimal root from first-order median vertex 2 to vertex 1. The theorem is not a small numerical improvement or arbitrary finite case.
